paper_title: More Tokens, Lower Precision Towards the Optimal Token-Precision   Trade-off in KV Cache Compression
caption: The results of layer-wise quantized pruning on Llama-3-8B-Instruct, with SnapKV as pruning method. We use 4 KV token 4-bit as baseline and report the relative change. Configurations are modified every 4 layers for the initial and final layers, while intermediate layers are reconfigured every 8 layers.
model_annotation:
The plot illustrates the relative change in performance for various configurations of layer-wise quantized pruning applied to the Llama-3-8B-Instruct model, utilizing SnapKV as the pruning method. The x-axis is labeled "Layer" and represents the different layer groups in the model with tick marks at intervals corresponding to specific ranges: Layer 1-4, Layer 5-12, Layer 13-20, Layer 21-28, and Layer 29-32. The y-axis is labeled "Relative Change" and operates on a linear scale ranging from -15% to 5%, with increments of 5% indicated by horizontal grid lines. 

There are five lines represented in the plot, each with distinct colors and styles to denote different configurations. The yellow line with circular markers represents "LB-Avg of 2×tokens, 8-bit," which shows a relatively stable performance around 0% throughout the layers. The red line with square markers denotes "LB-Avg of 1×tokens, 16-bit," displaying a decline to nearly -10% at Layer 13-20, then increasing slightly toward the end. The light blue line with circular markers signifies "RULER4k of 2×tokens, 8-bit," which starts near 0% and remains fairly consistent, reaching just below -5% at Layer 21-28 before increasing. The dark blue line with square markers indicates "RULER4k of 1×tokens, 16-bit," which starts at around -5%, declines to nearly -10% at Layer 5-12, and increases towards approximately 5% at the last layer group. The gray dashed line marks the baseline of "4×tokens, 4-bit," remaining constant at 0% across all layers.
